chunks.title: Data source: Lake County CD Plus permit layer (lake_cdplus_permits)
chunks.textForEmbedding:
Data source: Lake County CD Plus permit layer (lake_cdplus_permits)

One of the selected run's two permit sources, covering the unincorporated-county layer. It contains 17,915 features, 17,671 distinct permit numbers and 12,454 distinct parcels. Clermont is loaded separately from its eTRAKiT portal.
Roofing permits: 3,312. Open permits: 3,753. Open roofing permits: 247.
Join: the permit layer's Alternate_Key matches the NAL ALT_KEY column; the undashed PARCEL_ID matches the layer's Parcel_ID. Alternate_Key is the better join because it is populated on 100% of permit features.
Two measured limits: The county CD Plus layer is NOT a countywide permit archive. Two measured limits. First, jurisdiction: a spatial test of every permit parcel against the 14 Census city polygons puts 45 of 17,915 features (0.25%) inside any city limit, and those are Lake County government facilities that the county permits for itself. The layer is unincorporated Lake County only, and no municipality delegates permitting to the county. Mailing city is not a jurisdiction signal - 4,688 features carry a CLERMONT mailing address while sitting in unincorporated south Lake. Second, time: Permit_LastModDate spans 2025-09-09 to 2026-09-08, exactly a 365-day rolling window, and only 846 of 17,671 permits (4.8%) were issued before 2024-09-09. The layer publishes recently-modified permits, not history.
Contractor of record is NOT exposed by this layer. For unincorporated Lake County it lives on the county permit detail pages, which sit behind a Cloudflare managed challenge, so contractor_name remains null on every parcel where this layer is the only loaded permit source. Clermont's eTRAKiT portal is the separately harvested exception.
Endpoint: https://utility.arcgis.com/usrsvcs/servers/365d9a169bc34110a3db2157c76f6c95/rest/services/Individual/CDPermitParcels/MapServer/0. IN lists longer than about 50 values return HTTP 500, so paging is done by OBJECTID range.

chunks.title: Data source: contractor of record — PARTIAL, Clermont only (1 of 15 jurisdictions)
chunks.textForEmbedding:
Data source: contractor of record — PARTIAL, Clermont only (1 of 15 jurisdictions)

Contractor identity status: supported_partial.
Blocker: Contractor of record is gated for fourteen of fifteen jurisdictions, not for the county as a whole. The county CD Plus layer publishes no contractor field and every lakecountyfl.gov permit detail page sits behind a Cloudflare managed challenge; the thirteen other municipalities are blocked, unavailable or manual-only. Clermont is the exception and is harvested: its eTRAKiT detail pages render the full contact grid server-side to plain HTTP. contractor_name is therefore non-null on the Clermont parcels that join the roll and null everywhere else, with the jurisdictional truth in the coverage snapshot - never as a claim that the county has no contractors.
Consequence: contractor_name is a real selected-table column that is populated for parcels in Clermont and null on the rest of the county. Clermont is one of fifteen permitting jurisdictions in Lake County, so a contractor count is never countywide coverage and must never be reported as one.
Clermont's eTRAKiT portal is the one open route to contractor names anywhere in the county: its permit detail pages render the contact grid server-side to plain HTTP, and they are harvested. Every other jurisdiction is blocked, unavailable or manual-only.
Outside Clermont a null carries enrichment_status contractor_gated_403 and means 'no source covering this parcel publishes a contractor', not 'no contractor worked on this property'. On a Clermont parcel whose permits named nobody the token is contractor_absent_on_permit, which is an established absence - the source does carry contractors and named none.
For unincorporated Lake County, the route to contractor names is a Chapter 119 records request to the Lake County Office of Building Services for the complete CD Plus permit history including contractor of record.

For unincorporated Lake County, the route to contractor names is a Chapter 119 records request to the Lake County Office of Building Services for the complete CD Plus permit history including contractor of record.

chunks.title: Data source: Florida GIO statewide parcel centroids 2025 (fl_gio_parcel_centroid_2025)
chunks.textForEmbedding:
Data source: Florida GIO statewide parcel centroids 2025 (fl_gio_parcel_centroid_2025)

Florida DOR 2026 preliminary NAL is the parcel denominator; geometry comes from the Florida GIO statewide parcel-centroid 2025 FeatureServer, which publishes 210,935 Lake rows.
That is 4,871 fewer than the assessed roll (2.26%), because the centroid release is one roll year older than the 2026 roll.
Why the gap is acceptable: The canonical denominator is the DOR 2026 preliminary NAL (215,806 rows, measured). The geometry source is the Florida GIO statewide parcel-centroid 2025 release (210,935 Lake rows, measured), which is one roll year older, so parcels first assessed for 2026 - new splits, new condo units and new construction - have no 2025 centroid yet. Geometry is never used as the parcel denominator and never seeds a parcel; it only decorates a NAL row that already exists.
Consequence for the query table: latitude and longitude are null for parcels first assessed in 2026. Those rows remain in the selected run with null coordinates rather than being dropped, so a radius search silently excludes them unless requireCoordinates is understood.
Endpoint: https://services9.arcgis.com/Gh9awoU677aKree0/arcgis/rest/services/Florida_Statewide_Parcel_Centroid_Version/FeatureServer/0. Offset paging breaks past 20,000 rows, so the fetch uses ids-only plus OBJECTID ranges.

chunks.title: Data source: Florida DOR NAL 2026 preliminary tax roll (fl_dor_nal_2026p)
chunks.textForEmbedding:
Data source: Florida DOR NAL 2026 preliminary tax roll (fl_dor_nal_2026p)

The NAL roll is the canonical parcel source and the denominator for every coverage claim: 215,806 assessed parcels in Lake County.
It supplies address, owner name and mailing address, property and usage type, DOR use code, year built, livable area, building count, assessed / market / land / taxable value, and the two most recent sales carried on the roll.
Measured field coverage: year built known on 169,007 parcels, physical ZIP on 212,737, owner name on 215,620, 168,315 distinct owner names, 20,236 out-of-state owners.
Identifier: DOR Parcel ID (with Alternate Key as the permit join), format NN-NN-NN-NNNN-AAA-AAAAA (23 characters), where A is an uppercase alphanumeric block/lot character rather than a digits-only slot; ALT_KEY is 7 digits. Join rule: PARCEL_ID and ALT_KEY are both unique across all 215,806 NAL rows (measured: 215,806 distinct of each). ALT_KEY joins the CD Plus permit layer's Alternate_Key; the undashed PARCEL_ID matches the layer's Parcel_ID.
Limitation: only the current roll is published. There is no attribute-bearing historical roll before 2024F, so nothing on this source can prove ownership history.
Bulk download portal: https://floridarevenue.com/property/dataportal.

chunks.title: Data source: Florida DOR SDF 2026 preliminary sales file (fl_dor_sdf_2026p)
chunks.textForEmbedding:
Data source: Florida DOR SDF 2026 preliminary sales file (fl_dor_sdf_2026p)

Florida DOR SDF 2026 preliminary plus NAL SALE_YR1/SALE_YR2. 37,020 sale records covering 30,977 parcels.
Sale window published: 2025 to 2026 only.
Ten-year ownership tenure provable from the loaded and inspected DOR evidence: NO.
Evidence: In the inspected DOR sources, the NAL folder exposes 2026P alone, and both SDF and NAL SALE_YR1 span 2025-2026 only. The DOR Map Data archive publishes Lake parcel files back to 2005F, but they carry parcel geometry only - the 2010 Lake file was downloaded and its attribute table holds exactly two fields, CO_NO and PARCEL_ID, across 178,377 records. Attribute-bearing PAR files begin at 2024F. Ownership tenure beyond the 2025-2026 window cannot be proven from those inspected DOR files. The deliberately unused Lake property appraiser and unexamined sales history or archives remain unknown, not unavailable; this is not an absence claim about every published Lake source. The query table exposes no_recorded_sale_in_dor_window as an explicit lower bound and never claims a tenure length. This preserves the unknown-versus-unavailable distinction in the official kit's skills/use-oracle/reference/permit-evidence-preflight.md field evidence states.
Consequence for the query table: no_recorded_sale_in_dor_window is a lower bound on tenure, never a tenure length. A property with no sale in the window may have changed hands in 2019 and the loaded data cannot tell.

chunks.title: Data source: Florida Sunbiz corporate registration — NOT ingested for this run
chunks.textForEmbedding:
Data source: Florida Sunbiz corporate registration — NOT ingested for this run

Sunbiz corporate registration is a Florida statewide bulk source. It was historically not ingested for this run. Under the current official kit, Sunbiz is mandatory and unresolved: load and reconcile Sunbiz first, then an adequate official DBPR snapshot, before future permit harvesting (use-oracle's mandatory operating sequence and dbpr-license-ingest's adequacy gate). DOR TPP is not a substitute for this identity baseline, and owner execution approval alone is not a kit waiver. The kit's bulk data-download portal is Cloudflare-challenged from this egress. Sunbiz name search is reachable, but it is not the approved bulk ingest channel.
Consequence: has_sunbiz_tenant is a real selected-table column that is null for every row. Null means unknown/not established because Sunbiz was not ingested; it must never be rendered or interpreted as false or as 'no company is registered at this address'.
Business activity at an address is instead evidenced by business_account_count, from the DOR tangible-personal-property roll.

chunks.textForEmbedding:
Data source: Florida DOR TPP / NAP 2026 tangible personal property roll (fl_dor_tpp_2026p)

Florida DOR TPP (NAP) 2026 preliminary. 33,346 tangible-personal-property business accounts, carrying NAICS code, owner name and situs address.
Construction NAICS accounts: 1,883. Roofing contractors (NAICS 238160): 44.
Scope note: Loaded business facts come from the tangible-personal-property roll, which carries NAICS codes, owner names and situs addresses; it is not the corporate or licensing identity baseline. Sunbiz corporate ingest was historically not run and remains a mandatory unresolved prerequisite under the current official kit's skills/onboard-county/SKILL.md stage 6 and skills/use-oracle/SKILL.md mandatory operating sequence: Sunbiz first, then adequate official DBPR, before future permit harvesting. DOR TPP is not a substitute and no approved exception to that prerequisite is recorded.
This is evidence of business activity at a situs address, taken from the county's own tangible-property roll. It is not a business directory, not a tenant registry and not a corporate-registration source.
